chunks: You have come before Us all alone, as when you were created first, leaving behind all that We had bestowed on you. We do not see your intercessors with you who, you imagined, had partnership with you. Shattered lie your ties with them now, and gone are the claims you made.
ai.seo_question: What happens to intercessors and worldly blessings on the Day of Judgment according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Surah Al-An'am, this verse underscores the Shia theological emphasis on individual accountability by depicting the soul's solitary return to the Creator, stripped of communal or hierarchical intercessors. It serves as a critique of polytheistic claims, illustrating how false deities and expected mediators vanish, leaving the individual to face the consequences of their own deeds and abandoned blessings.
